correctness.rationale: The 1995 signless incidence matrix determinant criterion gives det=2^c exactly for spanning odd-unicyclic graphs. Intrinsic volume scaling is sqrt(n)/(2(n-1)!). For n divisible by 3 maximum graphs are triangle factors with no one-edge exchange, which rules out nonvertex equality by convex multilinearity. Else determinant cofactor expansion certifies 2D and 4D product equality families. Exact integer tests independently enumerate all 121553 n-edge subsets for 3<=n<=7, including counts 1,12,162,10,420; these tests do not substitute for arbitrary-n proof.

originality.rationale: The 1995 primary paper already implies the determinant values and numerical maximum, which are not claimed as new. The assessment concerns rigidity of all unrestricted equality configurations iff n divisible by 3, constructive multi-apex equality families otherwise, and exhaustive symmetry-type/count refinements of maximum vertex graphs. Full material of the 1995 paper and 2021 hypersimplex paper inspected; published results returned for the same polytope cover different invariants. Risk of earlier implicit/explicit optimizer-equality treatment remains.
residual_risks: The graph determinant theorem is fully prior; only equality mobility/rigidity and enumerations are candidate contributions.
An older unpublished or inaccessible equality classification may subsume the nonvertex criterion.
Not all historical secondary literature and the 2014 triangulation source were inspected in full; no global historical uniqueness claim.

value.rationale: A motivated natural equality-geometry question: determines for every second hypersimplex whether maximum-contained simplices must be vertex-supported, with rigid dimensions modulo 3 and explicit positive-dimensional 2- and 4-parameter product loci otherwise. Counts and orbit types clarify the finite optimizer skeleton. Although the determinant bound is classical, the rigidity/continuous-locus structural dichotomy is not the same numerical invariant.
